name: Read
description:
Read a local file, web URL, or lightweight resource. Use multiple Read calls if you need multiple files/resources. Local file output includes a @PATH#TAG snapshot header and line numbers unless :raw is used. Use path selectors to read specific line ranges. URL reads are fetched once into a session artifact cache, then selectors page over cached text without refetching.

Supported resource paths:
- local files, e.g. src/main.rs or src/main.rs:10-30
- http(s) URLs, e.g. https://example.com or https://example.com:20-60
- artifact://<id> for full truncated tool output
- skill://list and skill://<name> for available skills; local filesystem skills override built-in skills
- session://current, session://current/stats, session://current/messages, session://current/messages/all, session://current/artifacts

IMPORTANT - Prefer Grep over Read:
- When searching for specific local content, ALWAYS use Grep first — it returns only matching lines, never truncates, and keeps context small.
- Read loads entire files/resources into context, which rapidly inflates token usage. Use it ONLY when you already know exactly which lines you need (e.g. after a Grep located the target), or when you must understand the full file/resource structure.
- Grep with context provides enough surrounding lines to decide the target range; then use Read path selectors to get the @PATH#TAG header for Edit.patch.
- If a Read result is truncated (you see a truncation notice), do NOT re-read the same range — use Grep for local search, or use a narrower Read selector for URL/resource pagination.
- Use path selectors only when you already know the target line range (e.g. from a prior Grep or cached URL read).

path.description: File path, http(s) URL, or resource URL to read. Supports local paths, web URLs, artifact://<id>, skill://<name>, and session://current resources. Append path selectors such as :10-20, :10+5, or :raw for ranges/raw output.

name: Glob
description: Find files matching a single globset pattern. Default tool for file discovery. Use this instead of Bash commands like find, ls, or rg --files when you need file paths. Patterns are passed to the globset engine; use **/*.rs, **/*.docx, or **/*.* for recursive matches, and src/*.rs for one directory level. Use multiple Glob calls if you need multiple patterns.

pattern.description: Globset pattern, for example *.rs, **/*.rs, **/*.docx, **/*.*, or src/**/*.ts. Use **/ for recursive matches.

path.description: Optional directory to search from. Defaults to .

name: Grep
description:
Default tool for searching code and file contents. Use this instead of Bash commands like rg, grep, or find | xargs grep. Supports Rust regex patterns and returns file:line matches.
- Use context to identify the target range before editing
- Grep output does NOT authorize Edit; call Read on the exact target range to get the @PATH#TAG header
- Use glob to restrict file types or directories
- Use multiple Grep calls if you need multiple patterns

pattern.description: The Rust regular expression pattern to search for. For literal symbols, simple names usually work directly; escape regex metacharacters when needed.

path.description: File or directory to search in. Defaults to .

glob.description: Globset pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.rs", "**/*.docx", "src/**/*.ts", "*.{ts,tsx}"). Use **/ for recursive matches.

context.description: Number of lines before and after each match. Use this to choose the Read range for Edit.patch; Grep output itself does not provide an editable @PATH#TAG.

name: Write
description: Write a file to the local filesystem. Parent directories are created automatically if they don't exist (mkdir -p).

path.description: Path to the file to write

content.description: Content to write to the file

name: Edit
description: Edit an existing file using an anchored patch after a fresh non-raw Read. Edit requires patch; old_string/new_string is not supported. Copy the @PATH#TAG header from the latest Read of that file, or from the fresh header returned by the previous successful Edit. A snapshot tag becomes stale after any successful Edit or Write to the same file. Successful Edit returns a fresh @PATH#TAG and numbered lines around the change; use that new header for immediate follow-up edits in the shown range, or re-read the next target range. If modifying multiple ranges from one snapshot, combine them into one patch with multiple hunks. Keep ranges tight: cover only lines that actually change. Body rows are final content only, each prefixed with +; never include -old rows, original lines, or bare context lines. Do not use Edit for formatting, import sorting, whitespace cleanup, or reindent-only changes; run the project formatter once after semantic edits.

path.description: Path to the file to edit

patch.description:
Anchored line patch. The first non-blank line must be @PATH#TAG from a fresh Read output or from the previous successful Edit result. Supports replace N..M:, replace N:, delete N..M, delete N, insert before N:, insert after N:, insert head:, and insert tail:. Numbers refer to ORIGINAL snapshot lines and do not shift within one patch. Body rows are ONLY final new lines, each prefixed with +. NEVER include original lines, -old rows, or bare context lines. Example: @src/foo.rs#0A3B
replace 5..5:
+    return result
Combine same-file changes into one multi-hunk patch when they come from the same snapshot, and keep each range tight.

name: Bash
description: Execute a focused shell command in the current session working directory for build, test, git, package-manager, server, or other shell-only tasks. Do NOT use Bash for file discovery, code content search, or reading files when a dedicated tool fits: use Glob for paths, Grep for content search, and Read for known files or line ranges. Returns stdout and stderr.

command.description: The focused bash command to execute. Avoid search/read commands such as rg, grep, find, ls, or cat when Glob/Grep/Read can do the job.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds. If the command exceeds this duration, it will be killed. Only set this for commands expected to need a non-default duration (e.g. build, test, server start). Default: global tool timeout from configuration, clamped to 5-600 seconds.

name: Python
description: Execute Python code directly on the host system with full capabilities — network, subprocess, file system, and C extensions are all available. Returns stdout and stderr. Use this for data processing, analysis, or running helper scripts that need full Python ecosystem access. For sandboxed execution with restricted permissions, use PythonSandbox tool instead.

script_file.description: Path to a Python file to execute. Provide either 'script' or 'script_file', not both.

name: TodoWrite
description: Create and manage a structured task list for the current coding session. Use proactively for complex multi-step implementation, debugging, refactoring, review, or multi-file work. Do not use for trivial single-step or purely informational requests.

todos.description: The full updated todo list for the current session. Send the complete list each time, not a partial diff.

content.description: A short, concrete, actionable task description.

status.description: Task status: pending, in_progress, or completed. Prefer exactly one in_progress item while actively working.

name: PlanConfirm
description: Confirm and lock in the current plan draft. Call this ONLY when the user explicitly confirms the plan. Do NOT call this during drafting or when the user requests changes — only on explicit confirmation.

name: PlanClear
description: Clear the current plan. Call this when the current plan is fully completed and all tasks are done. After calling this, the system prompt will no longer include the plan section.

name: WebSearch
description:
Search the web using DuckDuckGo Lite with DuckDuckGo HTML fallback and return search results with titles, URLs, and snippets. If DuckDuckGo returns an anti-bot challenge, the tool reports that explicitly instead of returning empty results. Use this tool for accessing current information beyond your knowledge cutoff, such as recent events, latest documentation, or current data.

CRITICAL REQUIREMENT - You MUST follow this:
  - After answering the user's question, you MUST include a "Sources:" section at the end of your response
  - In the Sources section, list all relevant URLs from the search results as markdown hyperlinks: [Title](URL)
  - This is MANDATORY - never skip including sources in your response

name: WebFetch
description:
Fetches public content from a specified URL and returns readable text. Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content.

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: WebFetch WILL FAIL for authenticated or private URLs. Check if the URL points to an authenticated service (e.g. Google Docs, Confluence, Jira) before using.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - HTML is lightly extracted to text; non-HTML content is returned directly
  - Results may be truncated if the content is very large

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

name: SubAgent
description:
Launches a sub-agent that runs independently. The sub-agent executes the given prompt as an isolated agent session. Results are batched: ALL sub-agents complete before results are presented together. Use this for delegating sub-tasks that can run in parallel.

Fork mode: pass fork=true to inherit parent session context (conversation history, plan, skills). Default is a fresh independent session.

prompt.description: The prompt/task to delegate to the sub-agent

description.description: Short description of the sub-agent task (for logging)

fork.description: Set to true to inherit parent session context (conversation history, plan, skills). Default is false for a fresh independent session.

name: PythonSandbox
description: Execute Python code in a CPython WASI sandbox with restricted permissions — only specific directories have read/write access. No subprocess, no network, no C extensions. Full CPython standard library available (json/csv/re/math/datetime/xml etc.). Use this for safe execution of untrusted or sensitive Python code.

script_file.description: Path to a Python file to execute. Provide either 'script' or 'script_file', not both.
